      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

   879	The disjoint-union structure of \(\Pic_{C/k}\)
   880	(\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability}: a disjoint union of open
   881	quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes) may be indexed by the Hilbert polynomial
   882	\(\Phi \in \mathbb{Q}[\lambda]\) of a representing invertible sheaf
   883	(\cref{def:hilbert_polynomial}). If \(\mathcal H\) is a fixed ample
   884	invertible sheaf, Riemann--Roch gives
   885	\[
   886	  \chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H^{\otimes n})
   887	  = \deg\mathcal L+n\deg\mathcal H+1-g.
   888	\]
   889	Thus the leading coefficient is \(\deg\mathcal H\), whereas the intrinsic
   890	degree of \(\mathcal L\) is the constant-term difference
   891	\(\chi(C,\mathcal L)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)\). Equivalently,
   892	\(\deg\mathcal L\) is the leading coefficient of
   893	\(n\mapsto\chi(C,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})\). This identifies the connected
   894	components of \(\Pic_{C/k}(\overline k)\) with the integers, the index being
   895	the degree, without choosing a degree-one polarisation.

   897	\begin{definition}[Degree of a Picard class]\notready
   898	  \label{def:divisor_degree_pic}
   899	  \uses{def:pic_scheme, def:hilbert_polynomial, thm:fga_pic_representability,
   900	    def:has_pic_scheme}
   901	
   902	  % SOURCE: [Milne], ``Abelian Varieties'' (course notes, 2008),
   903	  % \S III.1, ``Definitions and main statements'', p.~88 (PDF p.~94)
   904	  % (read from references/abelian-varieties.pdf).
   905	  % SOURCE QUOTE:
   906	  % "Let \(C\) be a complete nonsingular curve over \(k\). The degree of a
   907	  % divisor \(D = n_i P_i\) on \(C\) is \(n_i [k(P_i):k]\). Since every
   908	  % invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C\) is of the form \(\mathcal{L}(D)\)
   909	  % for some divisor \(D\), and \(D\) is uniquely determined up to linear
   910	  % equivalence, we can define \(\deg(\mathcal{L}) = \deg(D)\). Then
   911	  % \(\deg(\mathcal{L}^n) = \deg(n D) = n \deg(D)\), and the Riemann-Roch
   912	  % theorem says that \(\chi(C, \mathcal{L}^n) = n \deg(\mathcal{L}) + 1 - g\).
   913	  % This gives a more canonical description of \(\deg(\mathcal{L})\): when
   914	  % \(\chi(C, \mathcal{L}^n)\) is written as a polynomial in \(n\),
   915	  % \(\deg(\mathcal{L})\) is the leading coefficient. We write
   916	  % \(\Pic^0(C)\) for the group of isomorphism classes of invertible sheaves
   917	  % of degree zero on \(C\)."
   918	  \textit{Source: [Milne], ``Abelian Varieties'' (course notes, 2008),
   919	  \S III.1, p.~88.}
   920	  Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus
   921	  \(g\) admitting a Picard scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\) as in
   922	  \cref{def:pic_scheme}. The \emph{degree map}
   923	  \[
   924	    \deg \;\colon\; \Pic_{C/k}(k) \longrightarrow \mathbb{Z}
   925	  \]
   926	  is defined as follows: a \(k\)-point \(\lambda \in \Pic_{C/k}(k)\)
   927	  represents (after \'etale base change) an invertible sheaf
   928	  \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C\). Its degree is characterised intrinsically by
   929	  Riemann--Roch as
   930	  \[
   931	    \deg(\lambda):=\deg\mathcal L
   932	    \;=\;\chi(C,\mathcal L)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C).
   933	  \]
   934	  Equivalently, \(\deg\mathcal L\) is the leading coefficient of
   935	  \(n\mapsto\chi(C,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})\). It is well-defined on the
   936	  isomorphism class \([\mathcal{L}]\) and (because \(\Pic_{C/k}\) represents the
   937	  \'etale-sheafified relative Picard functor) on the \(k\)-point
   938	  \(\lambda\). The degree map is a group homomorphism: for
   939	  \(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{M}\) invertible sheaves on \(C\) one has
   940	  \(\deg(\mathcal{L} \otimes \mathcal{M}) = \deg \mathcal{L} + \deg \mathcal{M}\),
   941	  by additivity of divisor degree. Equivalently, the degree on \(k\)-points is the index of the
   942	  connected component of \(\Pic_{C/k}\) containing \(\lambda\) under the
   943	  Hilbert-polynomial decomposition of
   944	  \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability}: the disjoint union
   945	  \(\Pic_{C/k} = \coprod_{d \in \mathbb{Z}} \Pic^d_{C/k}\) is indexed by
   946	  the degree, with \(\Pic^d_{C/k}\) the component representing classes
   947	  of degree \(d\).
   948	\end{definition}

    33	\section{Setup and motivation}
    34	\label{sec:pic0_setup}
    35	
    36	Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper
    37	geometrically integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) of genus \(g = g(C)\)
    38	(\cref{def:genus}). By
    39	\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and \cref{thm:pic_is_group_scheme}, the
    40	\'etale-sheafified relative Picard functor of \(C/k\) is represented by
    41	the \(k\)-group scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\) (\cref{def:pic_scheme}), which is
    42	separated, locally of finite type over \(k\), and a disjoint union of
    43	open quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes. The disjoint-union structure of
    44	\(\Pic_{C/k}\) stratifies its \(T\)-points by the Hilbert polynomial of the
    45	representing invertible sheaf relative to a fixed polarisation, and on
    46	the geometric points of the curve this stratification reduces to the
    47	degree of a line bundle.
    48	
    49	The identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) singled out by Kleiman is the open
    50	and closed subgroup scheme consisting of the connected component of
    51	\(\Pic_{C/k}\) containing the trivial line bundle. It is the locus of
    52	degree-zero classes, and on a smooth proper curve it is itself an
    53	abelian variety of dimension \(g\) --- the Jacobian variety of \(C\). This
    54	chapter packages those four statements as the A.3 specification.
    55

    57	\label{sec:identity_component_abstract}

    61	open-and-closed subgroup-scheme structure separately, so that the

body: 'Round 4 source correction: reviewer BLOCKED before commit


  The main formula and def:divisor_degree_pic downgrade are correct, but three affected
  repeats remain:


  1. blueprint Picard_IdentityComponent.tex:1168-1171 still calls deg(L) the leading
  coefficient of the fixed-polarisation Hilbert polynomial. For chi(L tensor H^n),
  that coefficient is deg H; degree is the constant-term offset. Correct this repeated
  proof occurrence.

  2. thm:pic_zero_k_points_iff_degree_zero remains leanok/lean-pinned and its Lean-encoding
  summary at 1244-1250 still claims the classical section-domain theorem. Exact Lean
  declaration has extra [ClassDegreePinned C] and [PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C],
  quantifies arbitrary underlying morphisms lambda/mu without section equations, uses
  the off-section-totalized degree, and is still sorry. This is the same signature
  mismatch as the degree node. Mark the node notready/remove the Lean pin and remove
  or explicitly downgrade the summary; do not leave a false signature match.

  3. IdentityComponent.lean:1707-1710 says “The degree map is a group homomorphism”
  inside the docstring of the totalized function. Only the pinned map on relative
  Picard classes is a homomorphism; the off-section totalization is not proved to
  be one. Qualify this as the intended/restricted degree, or state only what the declarations
  prove.


  Also tighten blueprint:893-895 to “geometric connected components of Pic_{C/k} base-changed
  to kbar,” not connected components of the set Pic(kbar), and describe an etale-local
  representing line bundle on C after base change rather than a line bundle on C itself.
  Please send the final two-file private-index diff before committing.'
